3633.subject: Chemistry
3633.text: Find the emf of the following cell reaction, given ${E}_{{Cr}^{3 +} / {cr}^{2 +}}^{0} = - 0. 72V$ and ${E}_{{Fe}^{2 +} / Fe} = 0- 0. 42V$ at $25 ° C$ is $Cr\left|{Cr}^{3 +} ( 0. 1M ) ‖ {Fe}^{2 +} ( 0. 1M )\right|Fe$
3633.sol:
The given cell is:

$Cr\left|{Cr}^{3 +} ( 0. 1M ) ‖ {Fe}^{2 +} ( 0. 1M )\right|Fe$

The half reactions can be written as:

$Cr \to {Cr}^{3 +} + 3e^{- 1}E^{°} = - 0. 72V{Fe}^{2 +} + 2e^{- 1} \to FeE^{°} = - 0. 42V$

The full reaction of the operating cell is:

$3{Fe}^{2 +} + 2Cr \to 2{Cr}^{3 +} + 3Fe$

Now, emf of the cell reaction is

$E^{°}cell = E^{°}cathode - E^{°}anodeE^{°}cell = - 0. 42 - ( - 0. 72 ) = 0. 30V$

Therefore,

${E}_{cell} = E^{°}cell - \dfrac{nRT}{F}lnQ$

${E}_{cell} = E^{°}cell - \dfrac{2. 303nRT}{F}\log_{10}\dfrac{\left[{Cr}^{3 +}\right]2}{\left[{Fe}^{2 +}\right]3}{E}_{cell} = 0. 3 - \dfrac{0. 059}{6}\log_{10}\dfrac{\left[0. 1\right]2}{\left[0. 1\right]3}{E}_{cell} \approx 0. 30V$

5065.sol:
Number of octahedral voids $=\mathrm{x}$ (where $\mathrm{x}=$ total number of atoms in the rinit cell)
Number of tetrahedral Voids $=2 \mathrm{x}\Rightarrow$ Total number of ' $A$ ' atoms $=x+2 x=3 x$
Since all 'B' atoms occupy all the FCC centres:-
\Rightarrow Total number of 'B' atoms $=\left[6 \times \frac{1}{2}\right]+\left[8 \times \frac{1}{8}\right]=4\Rightarrow \quad x=4$ so number of ' $A$ ' atoms $=3 x=3 \times 4=12$
So, the formula will be $A_{12} B_4$ or $A_3 B$

5479.text: Calculate the ratio of the effusion of \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \(\mathrm{N}_{2}\), when temperature and pressure gradients are held constant?
5479.sol:
The rate of effusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of the mass of its particles.
Rate of effusion \(\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\text{ Molecular mass }}}\)
If two gases \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \( \mathrm{N}_{2}\) are at the same temperature and pressure, the ratio of their effusion rates is inversely proportional to the ratio of the square roots of their molar masses.
\(\frac{\text{ Rate effusion of } \mathrm{CO}}{\text{ Rate of effusion of } \mathrm{N}_2} \propto \frac{\sqrt{M_{\mathrm{N}_2}}}{\sqrt{M_{\mathrm{CO}}}}
\(\Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{\frac{28}{28}} \Rightarrow1: 1\)
Hence,$ the correct option is (b). $

10181.text: If one end of focal chord of the parabola $y^{2} = 8x$ is $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, 2\right)$, then the length of the focal chord is____units
10181.sol:
Given parabola is ${y}^{2} = 8x$

By comparing with parabola ${y}^{2} = 4ax$

$a = 2$

Parametric point on parabola is $\left(a{t}^{2}, 2at\right) = \left(2{t}^{2}, 4t\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}, 2\right)$

$⇒ 4t = 2$

$t = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Length of focal chord will be $a{\left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)}^{2}$

$= 2{\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + 2\right)}^{2}$

$= 2 \times \left(\dfrac{25}{4}\right)$

$= \dfrac{25}{2}$

20071.subject: Chemistry
20071.text: What is the spin only magnetic moment of the metal ion in $\mathrm{P}$ and the oxidation number of Sulphur in the oxidised product $\mathrm{Z}$ ?
20071.sol:
Pyrolusite is $MnO_2$. When fused with $KOH$ and $KNO_3$, it forms potassium manganate ($K_2MnO_4$), which is compound $P$.

$2MnO_2 + 4KOH + O_2 \rightarrow 2K_2MnO_4 + 2H_2O$.

In $K_2MnO_4$, the manganese ion is $MnO_4^{2-}$. The oxidation state of $Mn$ is $+6$. The electronic configuration of $Mn^{6+}$ is $[Ar] 3d^1$.

The number of unpaired electrons $n = 1$. The spin-only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.732 \text{ BM}$.

Compound $P$ ($K_2MnO_4$) undergoes disproportionation in acidic medium to form $MnO_2$ (blackish brown, $X$) and $KMnO_4$ ($Y$).

$3MnO_4^{2-} + 4H^+ \rightarrow 2MnO_4^- + MnO_2 + 2H_2O$.

Thus, $Y$ is $MnO_4^-$. In neutral medium, $MnO_4^-$ reacts with thiosulphate $(S_2O_3)^{2-}$ to form $MnO_2$ and sulphate $(SO_4)^{2-}$.

$8MnO_4^- + 3S_2O_3^{2-} + H_2O \rightarrow 8MnO_2 + 6SO_4^{2-} + 2OH^-$.

The oxidised product $Z$ is $SO_4^{2-}$. In $SO_4^{2-}$, the oxidation number of sulphur is calculated as $x + 4(-2) = -2$, which gives $x = +6$.

Answer: $\mu=1.732 \mathrm{BM} \quad$ Oxidation number $=+6$

20405.subject: Chemistry
20405.text: Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their reactivity when each of them is reacted with chloroethane / anhydrous AlC$l_3$.
20405.sol:
The reaction of chloroethane with anhydrous $AlCl_{3}$ is a Friedel-Crafts alkylation reaction. This reaction is an electrophilic aromatic substitution where the benzene ring acts as a nucleophile. The reactivity of the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution depends on the electron density of the ring. Electron-donating groups increase the electron density and thus increase the reactivity, while electron-withdrawing groups decrease the electron density and decrease the reactivity.

Let us analyze the substituents on the benzene rings:
Compound [A] is benzene, which has no substituents.
Compound [B] is bromobenzene. The $-Br$ group is deactivating due to its strong inductive effect ($-I$) which outweighs its resonance effect ($+M$) in terms of overall reactivity towards electrophilic substitution.
Compound [C] is p-xylene (1,4-dimethylbenzene). The two $-CH_{3}$ groups are electron-donating via inductive effect ($+I$) and hyperconjugation, significantly increasing the electron density of the ring.
Compound [D] is nitrobenzene. The $-NO_{2}$ group is a very strong electron-withdrawing group due to both $-I$ and $-M$ effects, making the ring highly deactivated.

Comparing the reactivity:
Nitrobenzene [D] is the least reactive due to the strong deactivating $-NO_{2}$ group.
Bromobenzene [B] is less reactive than benzene [A] because $-Br$ is deactivating.
Benzene [A] is less reactive than p-xylene [C] because p-xylene has two activating methyl groups.

Therefore, the increasing order of reactivity is D < B < A < C.

Answer: D < B < A < C

21311.text: The function $x + y = \tan^{-1} y$ is the solution of which of the following differential equations?
21311.sol:
Given equation is $x + y = \tan^{-1} y$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$1 + y' = \dfrac{1}{1 + y^2} y'$

Multiplying both sides by $1 + y^2$:

$(1 + y')(1 + y^2) = y'$

$1 + y^2 + y' + y^2 y' = y'$

Subtracting $y'$ from both sides:

$y^2 y' + y^2 + 1 = 0$

Answer: $y^2 y' + y^2 + 1 = 0$

21698.text: Shade the feasible region for the inequations $6 x+4 y \leq 120,3 x+10 y \leq 180, x, y \geq 0$ in a rough figure.
21698.sol:
The given inequations are $6x + 4y \leq 120$ and $3x + 10y \leq 180$ with $x, y \geq 0$.

First, simplify the inequalities:
$6x + 4y \leq 120 \Rightarrow 3x + 2y \leq 60$
$3x + 10y \leq 180$

Find the intercepts for the lines:
For $3x + 2y = 60$:
If $x = 0$, $y = 30$. Point is $(0,30)$.
If $y = 0$, $x = 20$. Point is $(20,0)$.

For $3x + 10y = 180$:
If $x = 0$, $y = 18$. Point is $(0,18)$.
If $y = 0$, $x = 60$. Point is $(60,0)$.

Find the intersection point of the two lines:
$3x + 2y = 60$
$3x + 10y = 180$
Subtracting the first from the second: $8y = 120 \Rightarrow y = 15$.
Substituting $y = 15$ into $3x + 2y = 60$: $3x + 30 = 60 \Rightarrow 3x = 30 \Rightarrow x = 10$.
The intersection point is $(10,15)$.

The feasible region is bounded by the axes and the lines, specifically the polygon formed by the vertices $(0,0)$, $(20,0)$, $(10,15)$, and $(0,18)$. This matches the second image provided in the prompt.

Answer:

21996.subject: Mathematics
21996.text:
Consider an infinite geometric series with first term '$a$' and common ratio '$r$'.
If the sum of infinite geometric series is 4 and the second term is $\dfrac{3}{4}$ then
21996.sol:
The sum of an infinite geometric series is given by $S = \dfrac{a}{1-r} = 4$, where $|r| < 1$.

The second term of the series is $ar = \dfrac{3}{4}$.

From the first equation, $a = 4(1-r)$. Substituting this into the second equation:

$4(1-r)r = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$4r - 4r^2 = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$16r - 16r^2 = 3$

$16r^2 - 16r + 3 = 0$

Solving the quadratic equation using the quadratic formula $r = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$:

$r = \dfrac{16 \pm \sqrt{256 - 192}}{32} = \dfrac{16 \pm \sqrt{64}}{32} = \dfrac{16 \pm 8}{32}$

This gives two possible values for $r$:

$r_1 = \dfrac{24}{32} = \dfrac{3}{4}$ and $r_2 = \dfrac{8}{32} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

For $r = \dfrac{3}{4}$, $a = 4(1 - \dfrac{3}{4}) = 4(\dfrac{1}{4}) = 1$.

For $r = \dfrac{1}{4}$, $a = 4(1 - \dfrac{1}{4}) = 4(\dfrac{3}{4}) = 3$.

Comparing with the given options, the pair $a=3$ and $r=\dfrac{1}{4}$ matches option (3).

Answer: $a=3 \quad r=\dfrac{1}{4}$

22110.subject: Mathematics
22110.text: The angle between two lines is $45^{{}^{\circ}}$ and slope of one line is $\dfrac{1}{4}$ then which is the possible value of the slope of the other line.
22110.sol:
Let the slope of the first line be $m_1 = \dfrac{1}{4}$ and the slope of the second line be $m_2$. The angle $\theta$ between two lines with slopes $m_1$ and $m_2$ is given by the formula $\tan \theta = \left| \dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1 m_2} \right|$.

Given $\theta = 45^{{}^{\circ}}$, we have $\tan 45^{{}^{\circ}} = 1$. Substituting the values, we get $1 = \left| \dfrac{m_2 - \dfrac{1}{4}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{4} m_2} \right|$.

This simplifies to $1 = \left| \dfrac{4m_2 - 1}{4 + m_2} \right|$.

This leads to two cases:

Case 1: $\dfrac{4m_2 - 1}{4 + m_2} = 1 \Rightarrow 4m_2 - 1 = 4 + m_2 \Rightarrow 3m_2 = 5 \Rightarrow m_2 = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

Case 2: $\dfrac{4m_2 - 1}{4 + m_2} = -1 \Rightarrow 4m_2 - 1 = -4 - m_2 \Rightarrow 5m_2 = -3 \Rightarrow m_2 = -\dfrac{3}{5}$.

Comparing the results with the given options, the value $\dfrac{5}{3}$ is present.

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{3}$

22375.subject: Physics
22375.text: An AC voltage source of variable angular frequency $\omega$ and fixed amplitude $\mathrm{V}_0$ is connected in series with a capacitance $\mathrm{C}$ and an electric bulb of resistance $\mathrm{R}$ (inductance zero). When $\omega$ is decreased
options: total impedance of the circuit is unchanged
22375.sol:
The impedance $Z$ of an RC series circuit is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_C^2}$, where $X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$ is the capacitive reactance.

When the angular frequency $\omega$ is decreased, the capacitive reactance $X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$ increases.

Since $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + \left(\dfrac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2}$, an increase in $X_C$ leads to an increase in the total impedance $Z$ of the circuit.

The current $I$ in the circuit is given by $I = \dfrac{V_0}{Z}$. As $Z$ increases, the current $I$ decreases.

The power dissipated by the bulb is $P = I^2 R$. Since the current $I$ decreases, the power dissipated by the bulb decreases, causing the bulb to glow dimmer.

Answer: the bulb glows dimmer

Structure A is a hemiacetal (reducing sugar) that exists in equilibrium with its open-chain aldehyde form, allowing it to react with Tollen's reagent.

Structure C has a cyclic ether oxygen and lacks a free aldehyde group that can be generated under mild conditions, preventing reaction with Tollen's.
Structure D is a hemiacetal form of a reducing sugar with a free anomeric -OH, allowing equilibrium with the aldehyde form and reaction with Tollen's.
Structures B and C do not react with Tollen's reagent.

30202.subject: Chemistry
30202.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-I (Reaction)List-II (Mechanism)
A. Williamson SynthesisI. Electrophilic addition
B. Friedel Craft ReactionII. Free radical substitution
C. Bromination of vinyl benzeneIII. Nucleophilic substitution
D. Chlorination of toluene in lightIV. Electrophilic substitution

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
30202.sol:
Williamson synthesis involves the reaction of an alkyl halide with a sodium alkoxide to form an ether, which proceeds via a nucleophilic substitution ($S_N2$) mechanism. Thus, A matches with III.

Friedel-Crafts reaction involves the alkylation or acylation of an aromatic ring in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst, which proceeds via an electrophilic substitution mechanism. Thus, B matches with IV.

Bromination of vinyl benzene (styrene) involves the addition of bromine across the carbon-carbon double bond, which proceeds via an electrophilic addition mechanism. Thus, C matches with I.

Chlorination of toluene in the presence of sunlight (or UV light) involves the substitution of hydrogen atoms in the methyl group by chlorine, which proceeds via a free radical substitution mechanism. Thus, D matches with II.

The correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

31702.text:
The vapour pressure of $30 % \left(w / v\right)$, aqueous solution of glucose is ________ $mmHg$ at ${25}^{∘}C$.

[Given: The density of $30 % \left(w / v\right)$, aqueous solution of glucose is $1 . 2g{cm}^{– 3}$ and vapour pressure of pure water is $24mmHg$.]

31702.sol:
To calculate the vapour pressure of the $30 %$ (w/v) aqueous solution of glucose, we can use Raoult's law, which states that the vapour pressure of a component in an ideal solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the solution.

Weight of solution $= 100 \times 1 . 2 = 120gm$

Weight of water $= 120 - 30 = 90gm$

Now using formula

$\dfrac{{P}_{0} - P}{P} = \dfrac{molesof glucose}{molesof water}$

$\dfrac{24 - P}{P} = \dfrac{\dfrac{30}{180}}{\dfrac{90}{18}} = \dfrac{3}{90}$

$24 \times 90 - P \times 90 = 3P$

$⇒ P = 23 . 22$

34604.text:
The set of all values of $\lambda$ for which the system of linear equations:
$2 {x}_{1} - 2 {x}_{2} + {x}_{3} = \lambda {x}_{1}$
$2 {x}_{1} - 3 {x}_{2} + {2 x}_{3} = \lambda {x}_{2}$
$- {x}_{1} + {2 x}_{2} = \lambda {x}_{3}$
has a non-trivial solution,
34604.sol:
$\left(2 - \lambda\right) {x}_{1} - 2 {x}_{2} + {x}_{3} = 0$

$2 {x}_{1} - \left(\lambda + 3\right) {x}_{2} + 2 {x}_{3} = 0$

$- {x}_{1} + 2 {x}_{2} - \lambda {x}_{3} = 0$

The systems of linear equations will have a non-trivial solution

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}2 - \lambda & - 2 & 1 \\ 2 & - \lambda - 3 & 2 \\ - 1 & 2 & - \lambda\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(2 - \lambda\right) \left[{\lambda}^{2} + 3 \lambda - 4\right] + 2 \left[- 2 \lambda + 2\right] + 1 \left[4 - \lambda - 3\right] = 0$

$2 {\lambda}^{2} + 6 \lambda - 8 - {\lambda}^{3} - 3 {\lambda}^{2} + 4 \lambda - 4 \lambda + 4 + 1 - \lambda = 0$

$- {\lambda}^{3} - {\lambda}^{2} + 5 \lambda - 3 = 0$

${\lambda}^{3} + {\lambda}^{2} - 5 \lambda + 3 = 0$

$\left(\lambda - 1\right) \left({\lambda}^{2} + 2 \lambda - 3\right) = 0$

$\left(\lambda - 1\right) \left(\lambda + 3\right) \left(\lambda - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = -3 , 1 , 1$

34706.text: Let $x = x ( t )$ and $y = y ( t )$ be solutions of the differential equations $\dfrac{dx}{dt} + ax = 0$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt} + by = 0$ respectively, $a, b \in R$. Given that $x ( 0 ) = 2; y ( 0 ) = 1$ and $3y ( 1 ) = 2x ( 1 )$, the value of $t$, for which $x ( t ) = y ( t )$, is :
34706.sol:
Given: $\dfrac{dx}{dt} + ax = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{x} = - adt$

Integrating both sides,

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x} = - a ∫ dt$

$⇒ log | x | = - at + c$

At $t = 0, x = 2$

$⇒ log2 = 0 + c$

$⇒ logx = - at + log2$

$⇒ logx - log2 = - at$

$⇒ log\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = - at$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{2} = {e}^{- at}$

$⇒ x = 2{e}^{- at} . . . ( i )$

It is also given that, $\dfrac{dy}{dt} + by = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{y} = - bdt$

$⇒ log | y | = - bt + \lambda$

At, $t = 0, y = 1$

$⇒ 0 = 0 + \lambda$

$⇒ y = {e}^{- bt} . . . ( ii )$

According to question,

$3y ( 1 ) = 2x ( 1 )$

$⇒ 3{e}^{- b} = 2\left(2{e}^{- a}\right)$

$⇒ {e}^{a - b} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$\text{For}x\left(t\right) = y\left(t\right)$

$⇒ 2{e}^{- at} = {e}^{- bt}$

$⇒ 2 = {e}^{( a - b ) t}$

$⇒ 2 = {\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}^{t}$

$⇒ log\left(2\right) = t \times log\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)$

$⇒ log\dfrac{4}{3}2 = t$

34976.text: If the line $\alpha x+4 y=\sqrt{7}$, where $\alpha \in \mathbf{R}$, touches the ellipse $3 x^{2}+4 y^{2}=1$ at the point P in the first quadrant, then one of the focal distances of $P$ is :
34976.sol:
Ellipse $3x^2 + 4y^2 = 1$: $a^2 = \frac{1}{3}$, $b^2 = \frac{1}{4}$, $e = \frac{1}{2}$.
Tangent at $(x_0, y_0)$: $3x_0x + 4y_0y = 1$.
Comparing with $\alpha x + 4y = \sqrt{7}$:
$4y_0 = \frac{4}{\sqrt{7}} \Rightarrow y_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}$ and $3x_0 = \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{7}}$.
Substituting in ellipse equation: $\frac{\alpha^2}{21} + \frac{4}{7} = 1 \Rightarrow \alpha^2 = 9 \Rightarrow \alpha = 3$.
$P = \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\right)$.
Focal distances $= a \pm ex_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \pm \frac{1}{2\sqrt{7}}$.
One focal distance is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{7}}$.

36385.text: All words, with or without meaning, are made using all the letters of the word $MONDAY$. These words are written as in a dictionary with serial numbers. The serial number of the word $MONDAY$ is
36385.sol:
The given word is MONDAY

Arranging the letters alphabetically, we get

ADMNOY

When the word starts with any of the letters A/D, the number of possibilities$= 5 ! \times 2 = 240$

Now when the word starts with MA, then the number of possibilities$= 4 ! = 24$

Now when the word starts with MD, then the number of possibilities $= 4 ! = 24$

Now when the word starts with MN, then the number of possibilities $= 4 ! = 24$

Now when the word starts with MOA, then the number of possibilities$= 3 ! = 6$

Now when the word starts with MOD, then the number of possibilities $= 3 ! = 6$

Now when the word starts with MONA, then the number of possibilities $= 2 ! = 2$

Now when the word starts with MONDAY, then the number of possibilities$= 1$

Rank $= 240 + 24 \times 3 + 6 \times 2 + 2 + 1 = 327$

Hence, rank of the word MONDAY is $327$.

SHORTCUT METHOD

Another method is a shortcut, first number the alphabet and then check how many number are there on right hand side less that number and then start number in factorial in decreasing order and then multiply and add them and in last add one to find rank,

$\begin{cases}3 & 5 & 4 & 2 & 1 & 6 \\ M & O & N & D & A & Y \\ 2 & 3 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 ! & 4 ! & 3 ! & 2 ! & 1 ! & 0 !\end{cases}$

$∴$ Rank $= ( 2 \times 5 ! + 3 \times 4 ! + 2 \times 3 ! + 1 \times 2 ! )$

$= 240 + 72 + 12 + 2 + 1 = 327$

36541.text: The probabilities that players $A$ and $B$ of a team are selected for the captaincy for a tournament are $0.6$ and $0.4$, respectively. If $A$ is selected the captain, the probability that the team wins the tournament is $0.8$ and if $B$ is selected the captain, the probability that the team wins the tournament is $0.7$. Then the probability, that the team wins the tournament, is :
36541.sol:
Let $A$ be the event that player A is selected as captain, and $B$ the event that player B is selected as captain. Let $W$ be the event that the team wins the tournament.

Given:
$P(A) = 0.6$, $P(B) = 0.4$
$P(W \mid A) = 0.8$, $P(W \mid B) = 0.7$

By the law of total probability:
$P(W) = P(A) \cdot P(W \mid A) + P(B) \cdot P(W \mid B)$

$P(W) = (0.6)(0.8) + (0.4)(0.7)$

$P(W) = 0.48 + 0.28 = 0.76$

Hence, the correct option is $(2)\ 0.76$.

36717.subject: Mathematics
36717.text: In a random experiment, a fair die is rolled until two fours are obtained in succession. The probability that the experiment will end in the fifth throw of the die is equal to :
36717.sol:
The probability of getting a $4$ in a throw of a die is $\dfrac{1}{6}$.

The probability of getting other than $4$ i.e. $4$ i.e. numbers $1, 2, 3, 5 \text{ and } 6$ in a single throw of a die is $\dfrac{5}{6}$.

Total throws done $= 5$.

For the event to be completed in ${5}^{th}$ throw, ${4}^{th}$ and ${5}^{th}$ throw must be $4$ . Also, ${3}^{rd}$ throw must be other than $4$ i.e. $4$. Hence, cases for the first two position can be :

Case I : ${1}^{st}$ throw must be $4$ and ${2}^{nd}$ throw must not be $4$ i.e. $4$

Thus, $P\left(4\overset{-}{4}\overset{-}{4}44\right) = \dfrac{1}{6} . \dfrac{5}{6} . \dfrac{5}{6} . \dfrac{1}{6} . \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{25}{{6}^{5}}$.

Case II : ${1}^{st}$ throw must not be $4$ i.e. $4$ and ${2}^{nd}$ throw must not be $4$ i.e. $4$

Thus, $P\left(\overset{-}{4}\overset{-}{4}\overset{-}{4}44\right) = \dfrac{5}{6} . \dfrac{5}{6} . \dfrac{5}{6} . \dfrac{1}{6} . \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{125}{{6}^{5}}$.

Case III : ${1}^{st}$ throw must not be $4$ i.e. $4$ and ${2}^{nd}$ throw must be $4$

Thus, $P\left(\overset{-}{4}4\overset{-}{4}44\right) = \dfrac{5}{6} . \dfrac{1}{6} . \dfrac{5}{6} . \dfrac{1}{6} . \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{25}{{6}^{5}}$.

Therefore, probability that experiment will end in the fifth throw given that two fours occurred in succession will be

$P\left(4\overset{-}{4}\overset{-}{4}44\right) + P\left(\overset{-}{4}4\overset{-}{4}44\right) + P\left(\overset{-}{4}\overset{-}{4}\overset{-}{4}44\right)$

$= \dfrac{25}{{6}^{5}} + \dfrac{25}{{6}^{5}} + \dfrac{125}{{6}^{5}}$

$= \dfrac{175}{{6}^{5}}$.

For $0 < c < b < a$, let $( a + b – 2c ) {x}^{2} + ( b + c – 2a ) x + ( c + a – 2b ) = 0$ and $\alpha \ne 1$ be one of its root. Then, among the two statements

(I) If $\alpha \in \left(- 1, 0\right)$, then $b$ cannot be the geometric mean of $a$ and $c$.

(II) If $\alpha \in \left(0, 1\right)$, then $b$ may be the geometric mean of $a$ and $c$.
36860.sol:
Given: $f ( x ) = ( a + b – 2c ) {x}^{2} + ( b + c – 2a ) x + ( c + a – 2b )$

$⇒ f ( 1 ) = a + b – 2c + b + c – 2a + c + a – 2b = 0$

$⇒ f ( 1 ) = 0$

Using product of roots,

$⇒ \alpha \cdot 1 = \dfrac{c + a - 2b}{a + b - 2c}$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{c + a - 2b}{a + b - 2c}$

If, $- 1 < \alpha < 0$

Statement-I:

$⇒ - 1 < \dfrac{c + a - 2b}{a + b - 2c} < 0$

⇒ b + c < 2a and $b > \dfrac{a + c}{2}$

So, $b$ cannot be G.M. between $a and c$. $\left\{\text{as}A . M \ge G . M\right\}$

So, statement I is correct.

Statement-II:

$⇒ 0 < \alpha < 1$

$⇒ 0 < \dfrac{c + a - 2b}{a + b - 2c} < 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{c + a - 2b}{a + b - 2c} > 0 \text{$ and $} \dfrac{c + a - 2b}{a + b - 2c} < 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{c + a - 2b}{a + b - 2c} > 0 \text{$ and $} \dfrac{c + a - 2b - a - b + 2c}{a + b - 2c} < 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{c + a - 2b}{a + b - 2c} > 0 \text{$ and $} \dfrac{3c - 3b}{a + b - 2c} < 0$

$⇒ b < \dfrac{a + c}{2} \text{$ and } b > c  

Therefore, $b$ may be the G.M. between $a and c$. $\left\{\text{as}A . M \ge G . M\right\}$

So, statement II is also correct.

37443.text: For $\alpha \in N$, consider a relation $R$ on $N$ given by $R =${$\left(x, y\right): 3x + \alphay$ is a multiple of $7$}. The relation $R$ is an equivalence relation if and only if
options: $4$is the remainder when $\alpha$ is divided by $10$
$4$ is the remainder when $\alpha$ is divided by $7$
37443.sol:
Given, a relation $R$ on $N$ given by $R =${$\left(x, y\right): 3x + \alphay$ is a multiple of $7$},

Now for $R$ to be reflexive $⇒ xRx$

$⇒ 3x + \alphax = 7x$

$⇒ \left(3 + \alpha\right)x = 7K$

$⇒ 3 + \alpha = 7\lambda$

$⇒ \alpha = 7\lambda - 3 = 7N + 4, \left\{\text{where}K, \lambda, N \in I\right\}$

So, when $\alpha$ divided by $7$, remainder is $4$.

Now $R$ to be symmetric $xRy ⇒ yRx$

$3x + \alphay = 7{N}_{1}, 3y + \alphax = 7{N}_{2}$

$⇒ \left(3 + \alpha\right)\left(x + y\right) = 7\left({N}_{1} + {N}_{2}\right) = 7{N}_{3}$

Which holds when $3 + \alpha$ is multiple of $7$

So, $\alpha = 7N + 4$ (as did earlier)

Now, for $R$ to be transitive

$xRy \text{ and } yRz ⇒ xRz .

$⇒ 3x + \alphay = 7{N}_{1} . . . . $\left(1\right)$

$⇒ 3y + \alphaz = 7{N}_{2} . . . . . . \left(2\right)

And $3x + \alphaz = 7{N}_{3} . . . . . $\left(3\right)$

Now subtracting equation $\left(3\right)$ - $\left(2\right)$ we get,

$3x + 7{N}_{2} - 3y = 7{N}_{3}$

Now putting the value of $3x$ from equation $\left(1\right)$ we get, $7{N}_{1} - \alphay + 7{N}_{2} - 3y = 7{N}_{3}$

$⇒ 7\left({N}_{1} + {N}_{2}\right) - \left(3 + \alpha\right)y = 7{N}_{3}$

$⇒ \left(3 + \alpha\right)y = 7N$

Which is true again when $3 + \alpha$ divisible by $7$, i.e. when $\alpha$ divided by $7$, remainder is $4$ .

40907.text:
Statement I : The law of gravitation holds good for any pair of bodies in the universe.

Statement II : The weight of any person becomes zero when the person is at the centre of the earth.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement $1$ and statement $2$ both are true.
Statement $1$ is true and statement $2$ is false.
Statement $1$ and statement $2$ both are false.
Statement $1$ is false and statement $2$ is true.
40907.sol:
Gravitational force of attraction exists in all the places in the universe. This is the force of attraction between any two substances that are having a mass of their own.

Every object in the universe attracts every other object with a force which is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

The weight of a body placed at the centre of the earth is zero. This is because acceleration due to gravity is zero at the centre and hence weight $\left(mg\right)$ is zero at the centre. Thus, both statements are true.

41203.text:
A block of mass 5 kg is moving on an inclined plane which makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. Friction coefficient between the block and inclined plane surface is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. The force to be applied on the block so that the block will move down without acceleration is $\_\_\_\_$ N.
$\left(g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\right)$.
41203.sol:
For motion without acceleration, net force = 0.
Component of weight along incline: $mg\sin(30°) = 5 \times 10 \times 0.5 = 25$ N (down).
Normal force: $N = mg\cos(30°) = 50 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 25\sqrt{3}$ N.
Friction force opposing downward motion:
$f = \mu N = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 25\sqrt{3} = 37.5$ N (up).
For equilibrium along the incline, applying force F down the incline:
$mg\sin\theta + F = f$, so $25 + F = 37.5$, giving $F = 12.5$ N.

(Given, mass of electron $= 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31}kg$)
41518.sol:
Fiven that $\overset{\to}{E} = E\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{B} = 12\overset{^}{j}mT$

Kinetic energy$= 728eV$

Kinetic energy $= \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

$⇒ 728eV = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31} \times {v}^{2}$

$⇒ 728 \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31} \times {v}^{2}$

$⇒ v = 16 \times {10}^{6}m{s}^{- 1}$

For electron to move undeflected net force on it should be zero.

$⇒ eE = evB$

$⇒ E = vB = 16 \times {10}^{6} \times 12 \times {10}^{- 3}$

$⇒ E = 192 \times {10}^{3}V{m}^{- 1} = 192kV{m}^{- 1}$

43671.subject: Physics
43671.text: The temperature of a metal strip having coefficient of linear expansion $\alpha$ is increased from $T_1$ to $T_2$ resulting in increase of its length by $\Delta L_1$. The temperature is further increased from $T_2$ to $T_3$ such that the increase in its length is $\Delta L_2$. Given $T_3+T_1=2T_2$ and $T_2-T_1=\Delta T$, the value of $\Delta L_2$ is ______.
43671.sol:
Let the length of the metal strip at temperature $T_1$ be $L_1$.

When the temperature is increased from $T_1$ to $T_2$, the new length $L_2$ is given by:

$L_2 = L_1(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$

where $\Delta T = T_2 - T_1$.

The increase in length is:

$\Delta L_1 = L_2 - L_1 = L_1 \alpha \Delta T$

When the temperature is further increased from $T_2$ to $T_3$, the new length $L_3$ is:

$L_3 = L_2(1 + \alpha \Delta T')$

where $\Delta T' = T_3 - T_2$.

Given $T_3 + T_1 = 2T_2$, we have $T_3 - T_2 = T_2 - T_1 = \Delta T$.

Thus, $\Delta T' = \Delta T$.

The increase in length for this second temperature change is:

$\Delta L_2 = L_3 - L_2 = L_2 \alpha \Delta T$

Substituting $L_2 = L_1(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$ into the equation for $\Delta L_2$:

$\Delta L_2 = L_1(1 + \alpha \Delta T) \alpha \Delta T$

$\Delta L_2 = (L_1 \alpha \Delta T)(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$

Since $\Delta L_1 = L_1 \alpha \Delta T$, substituting this gives:

$\Delta L_2 = \Delta L_1(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$

Answer: $\Delta L_1[1+\alpha\Delta T]$

44337.text: The box of a pin hole camera, of length L, has a hole of radius a. It is assumed that when the hole is illuminated by a parallel beam of light of wavelength $\lambda$ the spread of the spot (obtained on the opposite wall of the camera) is the sum of its geometrical spread and the spread due to diffraction. The spot would then have its minimum size (say ${b}_{min}$ ) when:
44337.sol:
In diffraction, first minima, we have

$sin\theta = \dfrac{\lambda}{a}$

$b = a + \dfrac{L\lambda}{a} . . . \left(i\right)$

Then, minimum size of a spot, we get

$\dfrac{∂ b}{∂ a} = 0 ⇒ 1 - \dfrac{L\lambda}{{a}^{2}} = 0 ⇒ a = \sqrt{\lambdaL} . . . \left(ii\right)$

So,

${b}_{min} = \sqrt{\lambdaL} + \sqrt{\lambdaL}$

$= 2\sqrt{\lambdaL}$$= \sqrt{4\lambdaL}$

48676.text: The perimeter of a sector is a constant. If its area is to be maximum, then the sectorial angle is
48676.sol:
Let $r$ be the radius and $\theta$ be the sectorial angle. $\therefore$ Perimeter of sector,
$\begin{aligned} & k=2 r+\frac{\theta}{180^{{}^{\circ}}} \pi r \\ \Rightarrow \quad & r=\frac{k}{2+\frac{\theta \pi}{180^{{}^{\circ}}}} \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \therefore \text{ Area of sector, } \mathrm{A} &=\frac{\theta}{360^{{}^{\circ}}} \pi \mathrm{r}^{2} \\ &=\frac{\pi}{360^{{}^{\circ}}}\left[\theta \times\left(\frac{\mathrm{k}}{2+\frac{\pi \theta}{180^{{}^{\circ}}}}\right)^{2}\right] \\ \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{A} &=\frac{\mathrm{k}^{2} \pi}{360^{{}^{\circ}}}\left[\theta \times\left(2+\frac{\pi \theta}{180^{{}^{\circ}}}\right)^{-2}\right] \end{aligned}$
On differentiating w.r.t. ' $\theta$ ', we get

$\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{dA}}{\mathrm{d} \theta}=& \frac{\mathrm{k}^{2} \pi}{360^{{}^{\circ}}}\left[1 \times\left(2+\frac{\pi \theta}{180^{{}^{\circ}}}\right)^{-2}-2\left(2+\frac{\pi \theta}{180^{{}^{\circ}}}\right)^{-3}\right.\\
&\left.=\frac{\mathrm{k}^{2} \pi}{360^{{}^{\circ}}} \left(2+\frac{\pi \theta}{180^{{}^{\circ}}}\right)^{-2}\left[1-\frac{\pi}{180^{{}^{\circ}}}\right)\right]\\
&=\frac{\mathrm{k}^{2} \pi}{360^{{}^{\circ}}} \left(2+\frac{\pi \theta}{180^{{}^{\circ}}}\right)^{-3}\left[2-\frac{\pi \theta}{180^{{}^{\circ}}}\right]\\
\text{ Put }  \left.\frac{\mathrm{dA}}{\mathrm{d} \theta}=0 \Rightarrow 2-\frac{\pi \theta}{180^{{}^{\circ}}}\right]\\
\Rightarrow \quad \theta=\frac{2 \times 180^{{}^{\circ}}}{\pi}=2^{{}^{\circ}}
\end{aligned}

At \theta=2^{c}, \quad \frac{d^{2} \mathrm{ A}}{d \theta^{2}} <0$ (maximum)

51508.text: There are two candles of same length and same size. Both of them burn at uniform rate. The first one burns in 5 hours and the second one burns in 3 hours. Both the candles are lit together. After how many minutes the length of the first candle is 3 times that of the other?
51508.sol:
Let $\mathrm{V}_{1} \ \text{ and } \mathrm{ V}_{2}$ are rates of burning for both candles respectively $\ \text{ and } \mathrm{ L}$ is the length of each candle
$\mathrm{V}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{L}}{5} \quad \mathrm{ V}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{L}}{3}$
Let after time 't', their lengths are $\ell_{1} \& \ell_{2}\begin{array}{l}
\ell_{1}=\mathrm{L}-\frac{\mathrm{L}}{5} \mathrm{t} \\
\ell_{2}=\mathrm{L}-\frac{\mathrm{L}}{3} \mathrm{t} \\
\& \ell_{1}=3 \ell_{2} \text{ (Given) } \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{L}-\frac{\mathrm{L}}{5} \mathrm{t}=\left(\mathrm{L}-\frac{\mathrm{L}}{3} \mathrm{t}\right)^{3} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{5-\mathrm{t}}{5}=3-\mathrm{t} \\
\Rightarrow 5-\mathrm{t}=15-5 \mathrm{t} \\
\Rightarrow 4 \mathrm{t}=10 \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=2.5 \mathrm{hrs}=150 \mathrm{ min}
\end{array}$

56006.subject: Chemistry
56006.text: A first order reaction takes $16$ minutes for it's $50\%$ completion. What fraction that would react in $32$ minutes from the beginning?
56006.sol:
For a first order reaction, the half-life is given as $t_{1/2} = 16$ minutes.

The time given is $t = 32$ minutes.

The number of half-lives is $n = \dfrac{t}{t_{1/2}} = \dfrac{32}{16} = 2$.

The fraction of the reactant remaining after $n$ half-lives is $\dfrac{1}{2^n}$.

Fraction remaining $= \dfrac{1}{2^2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

The fraction of the reactant that has reacted is $1 - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{3}{4}$.

Answer: $3/4$

57096.subject: Chemistry
57096.text: Which from following gases causes the depletion of ozone layer in upper atmosphere?
57096.sol:
The ozone layer in the upper atmosphere is depleted by substances like chlorofluorocarbons and nitrogen oxides. Nitric oxide (NO) is a significant ozone-depleting agent that reacts with ozone ($\mathrm{O}_3$) in a catalytic cycle: $\mathrm{NO} + \mathrm{O}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{NO}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{NO}_2 + \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{NO} + \mathrm{O}_2$.

$\mathrm{O}_3 + \mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{O}_2$

NO acts as a catalyst, regenerating after each cycle to destroy multiple ozone molecules. Although other nitrogen oxides can contribute, NO is the most direct and potent among the options. The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{A}}$.

57616.text: Which from the following reaction is a Fittig reaction?
57616.sol:
Fittig reaction couples two aryl halides with sodium in dry ether to form diaryls. Analyzing each reaction:

A) $2\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_6 + 2\mathrm{NaCl}$ yields an alkane via the Wurtz reaction.

B) $2\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{Cl} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} (\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5)_2 + 2\mathrm{NaCl}$ produces a diaryl, matching the Fittig reaction.

C) $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{Cl} + \mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{Cl} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\cdot\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5 + 2\mathrm{NaCl}$ yields an alkylarene, characteristic of the Wurtz-Fittig reaction.

D) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl} + \mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{Cl} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5 + 2\mathrm{NaCl}$ yields an alkane via the Wurtz reaction.

57953.subject: Chemistry
57953.text: Calculate the pOH of $0.01$ M monobasic acid that is completely dissociated, at $298$ K.
57953.sol:
For a completely dissociated monobasic acid, the concentration of hydrogen ions is equal to the concentration of the acid.

$[H^+] = 0.01$ M $= 10^{-2}$ M

The pH of the solution is calculated as:

$\text{pH} = -\log[H^+] = -\log(10^{-2}) = 2$

At $298$ K, the relationship between pH and pOH is:

$\text{pH} + \text{pOH} = 14$

Substituting the value of pH:

$\text{pOH} = 14 - 2 = 12$

Answer: $12$

59555.text: A container contains equal masses of $\mathrm{H}_2, \mathrm{He}, \mathrm{CO}_2$ and Ne at a certain temperature. Which of the following gases exerts minimum partial pressure?
59555.sol:
According to Dalton’s law, the partial pressure of a gas is proportional to its mole fraction, or equivalently, to its number of moles when volume and temperature are constant. Given equal masses $m$ of $\mathrm{H}_2$, $\mathrm{He}$, $\mathrm{CO}_2$, and $\mathrm{Ne}$, the number of moles for each is calculated as $n = \frac{m}{M}$, where $M$ is the molar mass.

The molar masses are $M_{\mathrm{H}_2} = 2 \, \text{g/mol}$, $M_{\mathrm{He}} = 4 \, \text{g/mol}$, $M_{\mathrm{CO}_2} = 44 \, \text{g/mol}$, and $M_{\mathrm{Ne}} = 20 \, \text{g/mol}$. Thus, the moles are $n_{\mathrm{H}_2} = \frac{m}{2}$, $n_{\mathrm{He}} = \frac{m}{4}$, $n_{\mathrm{CO}_2} = \frac{m}{44}$, and $n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \frac{m}{20}$.

Since $m$ is constant, the number of moles is inversely proportional to molar mass. The largest molar mass belongs to $\mathrm{CO}_2$ ($44 \, \text{g/mol}$), so it has the smallest number of moles and therefore the minimum partial pressure.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

60241.text: The minimum value of $\mathrm{a} x+$ by where $x \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{c}^2$ is
60241.sol:
Given $E = ax + by$ with constraint $xy = c^2$. Expressing $y = \frac{c^2}{x}$, we obtain $E(x) = ax + \frac{bc^2}{x}$.

Differentiating yields $E'(x) = a - \frac{bc^2}{x^2}$. Setting $E'(x) = 0$ gives $x^2 = \frac{bc^2}{a}$, so $x = \pm c\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}$.

For $x = c\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}$, $y = c\sqrt{\frac{a}{b}}$, and $E = 2c\sqrt{ab}$. For $x = -c\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}$, $y = -c\sqrt{\frac{a}{b}}$, and $E = -2c\sqrt{ab}$.

The second derivative $E''(x) = \frac{2bc^2}{x^3}$ shows the first gives a local minimum and the second a local maximum. Since $E(x) \to -\infty$ as $x \to 0^-$ or $x \to -\infty$, no global minimum exists, but the minimal local extremum is $-2c\sqrt{ab}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

61059.subject: Mathematics
61059.sol:
The integral is separated into even and odd components:

$I = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} x^2 \, \mathrm{d}x + \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \log\left(\frac{\pi-x}{\pi+x}\right) \cos x \, \mathrm{d}x$

Since $x^2$ is even, the first integral evaluates to twice the integral from $0$ to $\pi/2$:

$2 \int_0^{\pi/2} x^2 \, \mathrm{d}x = 2 \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_0^{\pi/2} = \frac{\pi^3}{12}$

The second integrand is odd, as $\log\left(\frac{\pi+x}{\pi-x}\right) \cos x = -\log\left(\frac{\pi-x}{\pi+x}\right) \cos x$, leading to cancellation over symmetric limits. Hence, the integral is zero.

Combining the results yields $I = \frac{\pi^3}{12} + 0 = \frac{\pi^3}{12}$.

61303.subject: Mathematics
61303.text: The differential equation representing the family of curves $x \sin x + y^3 = 4ax$ is
61303.sol:
The given equation of the family of curves is $x \sin x + y^3 = 4ax$.

Dividing the entire equation by $x$, we get:

$\sin x + \dfrac{y^3}{x} = 4a$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain:

$\cos x + \dfrac{3y^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} \cdot x - y^3 \cdot 1}{x^2} = 0$

Multiplying the equation by $x^2$ gives:

$x^2 \cos x + 3xy^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} - y^3 = 0$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:

$3xy^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} = y^3 - x^2 \cos x$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^3 - x^2 \cos x}{3xy^2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^3 - x^2 \cos x}{3xy^2}$

61431.text: The differential equation of all circles which pass through the origin and whose centres lie on $\mathrm{Y}$-axis is
61431.sol:
Circle passes through origin and centre lie on $\mathrm{Y}$-axis.
Let $(0, k)$ be centre and ' $k$ ' be radius
$\therefore \quad$ Equation of circle is
$\begin{aligned}
& (x-0)^2+(y-\mathrm{k})^2=\mathrm{k}^2 \\
& x^2+y^2-2 y \mathrm{k}+\mathrm{k}^2=\mathrm{k}^2 \\
& x^2+y^2-2 \mathrm{k} y=0 \\
& x^2+y^2=2 \mathrm{k} y ...(i)\\
& \frac{x^2+y^2}{2 y}=\mathrm{k} ...(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Differentiating equation (i) with respect to $x$, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& 2 x+2 y \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=2 \mathrm{k} \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x} \\
& 2 x+2 y \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}-2 \mathrm{k} \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=0 \\
& 2 x+2(y-\mathrm{k}) \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=0 \\
& 2 x+2\left[y-\left(\frac{x^2+y^2}{2 y}\right)\right] \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=0 ...[From(ii)]\\
& 2 x+2\left[\frac{2 y^2-x^2-y^2}{2 y}\right] \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=0 \\
& 2 x+\left(\frac{y^2-x^2}{y}\right) \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=0 \\
& 2 x y+\left(y^2-x^2\right) \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=0 \\
& \text{ i.e. }\left(x^2-y^2\right) \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}-2 x y=0
\end{aligned}$

61654.sol:
Using the standard trigonometric identity $\cos x \cos 2x \cos 4x \dots \cos 2^{n-1}x = \dfrac{\sin 2^n x}{2^n \sin x}$, we can simplify the given function for $n=5$:

$f(x) = \dfrac{\sin 32x}{32 \sin x}$

Differentiating $f(x)$ with respect to $x$ using the quotient rule:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{32 \cos 32x \cdot 32 \sin x - \sin 32x \cdot 32 \cos x}{(32 \sin x)^2}$

$f'(x) = \dfrac{32 \cos 32x \sin x - \sin 32x \cos x}{32 \sin^2 x}$

Substituting $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$:

$32x = 32 \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 8\pi$

We know that $\sin 8\pi = 0$, $\cos 8\pi = 1$, and $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

$f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{32(1)\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) - 0}{32 \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2}$

$f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\dfrac{32}{\sqrt{2}}}{\dfrac{32}{2}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}$

Answer: $\sqrt{2}$

62568.subject: Mathematics
62568.text: The derivative of $\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{1+x^2}-1}{x}\right)$ w.r.t. $\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x \sqrt{1-x^2}}{1-2 x^2}\right)$ at $x=0$ is
62568.sol:
Let $u = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{1+x^2}-1}{x}\right)$ and $v = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2x\sqrt{1-x^2}}{1-2x^2}\right)$.
To find $\frac{du}{dv}$ at $x=0$, first simplify both expressions using trigonometric substitutions.

Substitute $x = \tan\theta$ for $u$:
$u = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{1+\tan^2\theta}-1}{\tan\theta}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sec\theta-1}{\tan\theta}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1-\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\right)$.

Using half-angle identities $1-\cos\theta = 2\sin^2(\theta/2)$ and $\sin\theta = 2\sin(\theta/2)\cos(\theta/2)$:
$u = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2\sin^2(\theta/2)}{2\sin(\theta/2)\cos(\theta/2)}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\tan(\theta/2)\right) = \frac{\theta}{2}$.

Since $\theta = \tan^{-1}x$, we have $u = \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}x$, and $\frac{du}{dx} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{1+x^2}$.

Now substitute $x = \sin\phi$ for $v$:
$v = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2\sin\phi\sqrt{1-\sin^2\phi}}{1-2\sin^2\phi}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2\sin\phi\cos\phi}{\cos2\phi}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sin2\phi}{\cos2\phi}\right) = \tan^{-1}(\tan2\phi) = 2\phi$.

Since $\phi = \sin^{-1}x$, we have $v = 2\sin^{-1}x$, and $\frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.

By the chain rule, $\frac{du}{dv} = \frac{du/dx}{dv/dx} = \frac{1/(2(1+x^2))}{2/\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \frac{\sqrt{1-x^2}}{4(1+x^2)}$.

At $x=0$:
$\left.\frac{du}{dv}\right|_{x=0} = \frac{\sqrt{1-0^2}}{4(1+0^2)} = \frac{1}{4}$.

The derivative $\frac{du}{dv}$ evaluated at $x=0$ is $\frac{1}{4}$.

63625.subject: Mathematics
63625.text: A family has 3 children. The probability that all the three children are girls, given that at least one of them is a girl is
63625.sol:
The sample space for the genders of three children contains all possible combinations of boys (B) and girls (G), yielding $2^3 = 8$ outcomes: S = {BBB, BBG, BGB, BGG, GBB, GBG, GGB, GGG}.

Let A be the event that all three children are girls, so A = {GGG} and $n(A) = 1$.

Let B be the event that at least one child is a girl. The complement B' consists of all three boys: B' = {BBB} and $n(B') = 1$, hence $n(B) = 8 - 1 = 7$.

The conditional probability $P(A|B) = P(A \cap B) / P(B)$. Since A $\subset$ B, $A \cap B = A$ and $n(A \cap B) = 1$. With $P(A \cap B) = 1/8$ and $P(B) = 7/8$, it follows that $P(A|B) = (1/8) / (7/8) = 1/7$.

The probability is $1/7$.

& \therefore(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c})=\frac{2(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c})}{\mathrm{k}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=2 \\

64397.text: The plane $\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{y}{3} + \dfrac{z}{4} =1$ cuts the co-ordinate axes at the points A, B, C respectively. Then the area of triangle ABC is
64397.sol:
The equation of the plane is given by $\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{y}{3} + \dfrac{z}{4} = 1$.

The intercepts on the coordinate axes are $a = 2$, $b = 3$, and $c = 4$.

The coordinates of the points where the plane cuts the axes are $A(2, 0, 0)$, $B(0, 3, 0)$, and $C(0, 0, 4)$.

The area of the triangle $ABC$ can be found using the areas of its projections on the coordinate planes, denoted as $\Delta_{xy}$, $\Delta_{yz}$, and $\Delta_{zx}$.

$\Delta_{xy} = \dfrac{1}{2}ab = \dfrac{1}{2}(2)(3) = 3$

$\Delta_{yz} = \dfrac{1}{2}bc = \dfrac{1}{2}(3)(4) = 6$

$\Delta_{zx} = \dfrac{1}{2}ca = \dfrac{1}{2}(4)(2) = 4$

The total area of the triangle is given by $\Delta = \sqrt{\Delta_{xy}^2 + \Delta_{yz}^2 + \Delta_{zx}^2}$.

$\Delta = \sqrt{3^2 + 6^2 + 4^2}$

$\Delta = \sqrt{9 + 36 + 16} = \sqrt{61}$ sq. units.

Answer: $\sqrt{61}$ sq. units

65060.text: If $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ are three non-coplanar vectors and $\vec{p}, \vec{q}, \vec{r}$ are defined as $\vec{p} = \dfrac{\vec{b} \times \vec{c}}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}, \vec{q} = \dfrac{\vec{c} \times \vec{a}}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}, \vec{r} = \dfrac{\vec{a} \times \vec{b}}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}$, then $[(\vec{a} + \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{p} + (\vec{b} + \vec{c}) \cdot \vec{q} + (\vec{c} + \vec{a}) \cdot \vec{r}]$ is equal to
65060.sol:
The given vectors $\vec{p}, \vec{q}, \vec{r}$ are the reciprocal vectors of $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$.

Using the properties of reciprocal vectors, we have:
$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{p} = \dfrac{\vec{a} \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]} = \dfrac{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]} = 1$
$\vec{b} \cdot \vec{p} = \dfrac{\vec{b} \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]} = 0$

Similarly, for the other dot products:
$\vec{b} \cdot \vec{q} = 1$, $\vec{c} \cdot \vec{q} = 0$
$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{r} = 1$, $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{r} = 0$

Expanding the given expression:
$(\vec{a} + \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{p} + (\vec{b} + \vec{c}) \cdot \vec{q} + (\vec{c} + \vec{a}) \cdot \vec{r}$

$= (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{p} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{p}) + (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{q} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{q}) + (\vec{c} \cdot \vec{r} + \vec{a} \cdot \vec{r})$

Substituting the values obtained above:
$= (1 + 0) + (1 + 0) + (1 + 0)$

$= 1 + 1 + 1 = 3$

Answer: $3$

66539.subject: Physics
66539.text: In photoelectric effect, keeping the frequency of incident radiation and accelerating potential fixed, if the intensity of incident light is increased,
options: the kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons increases.
kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons decreases.
66539.sol:
In the photoelectric effect, the intensity of incident light is directly proportional to the number of photons incident per unit area per unit time.

Increasing the intensity of the incident light increases the number of photons striking the metal surface per second.

Since the frequency of the incident radiation is kept fixed, the energy of each individual photon (E = h\nu$) remains constant. Therefore, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons (K_\max = h\nu - \Phi$) does not change.

However, a larger number of incident photons results in a larger number of photoelectrons being emitted per second.

This increase in the rate of emission of photoelectrons leads to an increase in the photoelectric current.

Answer: the photoelectric current increases.

68118.text: The excess pressure inside the first soap bubble of radius $R_1$ is three times that inside the second soap bubble of radius $R_2$. The ratio of volumes of the first to second bubble is
68118.sol:
The excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius $R$ is given by $\Delta P = \dfrac{4T}{R}$, where $T$ is the surface tension.

Given that the excess pressure inside the first bubble is three times that inside the second bubble:

$\Delta P_1 = 3 \Delta P_2$

$\dfrac{4T}{R_1} = 3 \left(\dfrac{4T}{R_2}\right)

\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{1}{3}

The volume of a spherical bubble is $ V = $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi$ R^3$. The ratio of their volumes is:

\dfrac{V_1}{V_2} = \left(\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}\right)^3$

$\dfrac{V_1}{V_2} =\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^3 = \dfrac{1}{27}

The ratio of volumes of the first to the second bubble is 1 : 27$.

Answer: $1 : 27$

68950.subject: Physics
68950.text: In the phenomenon of refraction of light for the same angle of incidence
options: angle of refraction is same for different colours.
angle of refraction is different for different colours.
angle of refraction does not depend upon the colour of the light used.
angle of refraction depends on critical angle.
68950.sol:
According to Snell's law, $\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \mu$, where $\mu$ is the refractive index of the medium.

The refractive index of a medium depends on the wavelength of light according to Cauchy's relation $\mu = A + \dfrac{B}{\lambda^2}$.

Since different colours of light have different wavelengths, the refractive index $\mu$ is different for different colours.

Therefore, for a given angle of incidence $i$, the angle of refraction $r$ will be different for different colours.

Answer: angle of refraction is different for different colours.

69436.subject: Physics
69436.text: A pure silicon crystal at temperature $300$ K has electron and hole concentration (n_i$) 10^{16}$ per m^3$ each and $10^{21}$ phosphorus atoms (n_e$) are added per cubic metre. The new hole concentration in silicon crystal is
69436.sol:
According to the mass action law for semiconductors:

$n_e n_h = n_i^2$

Given the intrinsic carrier concentration $n_i = 10^{16}$ m^{-3}$.

Phosphorus is a pentavalent impurity, which acts as a donor. Since the number of donor atoms added is much greater than the intrinsic concentration, the new electron concentration is approximately equal to the donor concentration:

$n_e \approx N_D = 10^{21}$ m^{-3}$

Substituting the values into the mass action law to find the new hole concentration $n_h$:

$n_h = \dfrac{n_i^2}{n_e}$

$n_h = \dfrac{(10^{16})^2}{10^{21}}$

$n_h = \dfrac{10^{32}}{10^{21}} = 10^{11}$ m^{-3}$

Answer: 10^{11}$ per m^3

For a receding light source, the relativistic Doppler shift formula simplifies to $\frac{\Delta\lambda}{\lambda} = \frac{v}{c}$ when $v \ll c$.

Substituting values: $\frac{v}{c} = 0.0002$

$v = 0.0002 \times 3 \times 10^8\ \mathrm{m/s} = 6 \times 10^4\ \mathrm{m/s}$

Converting to kilometers per second: $v = 60\ \mathrm{km/s}$

This result corresponds to option B.

71153.subject: Biology
71153.text: The antigen binding site of the antibody is formed of ______.
options: variable and constant regions of light chain
variable and constant regions of heavy chain
variable regions of both light and heavy chains
constant regions of both light and heavy chains
71153.sol:
An antibody molecule is composed of four polypeptide chains: two identical light chains and two identical heavy chains.

Each chain consists of a variable region at its N-terminal end and a constant region at its C-terminal end.

The variable regions of both the light and heavy chains come together to form the antigen binding site (paratope), which is highly specific for a particular antigen.

Therefore, the antigen binding site of the antibody is formed of the variable regions of both light and heavy chains.

Answer: variable regions of both light and heavy chains

71950.subject: Chemistry
71950.text: What type of the following defect is produced when NaCl crystal is doped with $\text{MgCl}_2$?
71950.sol:
When NaCl crystal is doped with $\text{MgCl}_2$, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ions replace $\text{Na}^+$ ions in the crystal lattice.

To maintain electrical neutrality, one $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ion replaces two $\text{Na}^+$ ions. One $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ion occupies the site of one $\text{Na}^+$ ion, leaving the other site vacant, which creates a cation vacancy.

Since a foreign ion is introduced into the host crystal, this type of defect is known as an impurity defect.

Answer: Impurity defect

72197.subject: Physics
72197.text: A parallel-plate capacitor of $50\ \mu\text{F}$ contains a dielectric slab of constant ($k$) with the same dimensions. If a time-varying potential difference is applied at a rate of $50\ \text{V/s}$. What is the displacement current in the capacitor?
72197.sol:
The displacement current $I_d$ in a capacitor is equal to the conduction current $I_c$ flowing into it.

$I_d = I_c = \dfrac{dQ}{dt}$

Since $Q = CV$, we have:

$I_d = C \dfrac{dV}{dt}$

Given:
$C = 50\ \mu\text{F} = 50 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{F}$
$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 50\ \text{V/s}$

Substituting the values:

$I_d = 50 \times 10^{-6} \times 50$

$I_d = 2500 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{A}$

$I_d = 2.5 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{A} = 2.5\ \text{mA}$

Answer: $2.5\ \text{mA}$

72248.text: A circular coil having 'n' turns, each of radius 'r' carries a current 'I'. The magnetic field at a distance $x = \sqrt{8}\ r$ from its centre along axis of the coil is $(\mu_0 = $ permeability of free space)
72248.sol:
The magnetic field at a distance $x$ on the axis of a circular coil of $n$ turns, radius $r$, carrying current $I$ is given by

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I r^2}{2(r^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$

Given $x = \sqrt{8} r$, substituting this value in the formula:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I r^2}{2(r^2 + (\sqrt{8} r)^2)^{3/2}}$

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I r^2}{2(r^2 + 8r^2)^{3/2}}$

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I r^2}{2(9r^2)^{3/2}}$

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I r^2}{2(27r^3)}$

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I}{54 r}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\mu_0 nI}{54\ r}$

72509.text: A transverse wave is described by the equation $y = A \sin 2\pi \left(nt - \dfrac{x}{10}\right).$ The ratio of maximum particle velocity to wave velocity is
72509.sol:
The given wave equation is $y = A \sin 2\pi \left($ nt - $\dfrac{x}{10}\right)

Comparing this with the standard wave equation $ y = A \sin($\omega$ t - kx)$, we get:

Angular frequency, \omega =2\pi$ n$

Wave number, $k = $\dfrac{2\pi}{10} = \dfrac{\pi}{5}

Maximum particle velocity is given by $ v_{p,max} = A$\omega =A(2\pi$ n)$

Wave velocity is given by $v_w = $\dfrac{\omega}{k} = \dfrac{2\pi n}{\pi/5} =10n$

The ratio of maximum particle velocity to wave velocity is:

$\dfrac{v_{p,max}}{v_w} = \dfrac{A(2\pi n)}{10n} = \dfrac{\pi A}{5}

Answer: \dfrac{\pi A}{5}$

74639.subject: General Ability
74639.text:
Which one among the following does not wet the walls of
the glass vessel in which it is kept ?
74639.sol:
Mercury in a glass flask is a good example of the effects
of the ratio between cohesive and adhesive forces.
Because of its high cohesion and low adhesion to the
glass, mercury does not spread out to cover the top of
the flask, and if enough is placed in the flask to cover
the bottom, it exhibits a strongly convex meniscus,
whereas the meniscus of water is concave. Mercury will
not wet the glass, unlike water and many other liquids,
and if the glass is tipped, it will 'roll' around inside.

82301.subject: Physics
82301.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
82301.text: Bob $B$ of mass $m$ at rest is hanging vertically from the ceiling via a massless string of length $10$ m, as shown in the figure. Point mass $A$ of mass $m$ travelling horizontally with speed $10$ ms$^{-1}$ hits bob $B$ elastically. The bob $B$ rises $h$ meter after the collision. Taking the acceleration due to gravity $g=10$ ms$^{-2}$ and neglecting the size of the bob, the value of $h$ is :
82301.sol:
Since the collision is elastic and the masses of $A$ and $B$ are equal, they will exchange their velocities upon collision.

Velocity of bob $B$ just after the collision, $v = 10$ ms$^{-1}$.

By conservation of mechanical energy for bob $B$ during its upward swing:

$\dfrac{1}{2} m v^2 = m g h$

Substituting the given values ($v = 10$ ms$^{-1}$, $g = 10$ ms$^{-2}$):

$\dfrac{1}{2} \times m \times (10)^2 = m \times 10 \times h$

$50 = 10 h$

$h = 5$ m.

Since $h < L$ (where $L = 10$ m), the string does not become slack and the bob reaches a maximum height of $5$ m.

Answer: $5$

84379.subject: Zoology
84379.text: Which one of the following sequences was proposed by Darwin and Wallace for organic evolution?
options: overproduction, variations, constancy of population size, natural selection
variations, constancy of population size, overproduction, natural selection
overproduction, constancy of population size, variations, natural selection
variations, natural selection, overproduction,constancy of population size
84379.sol:
Overproduction, variations, the constancy of population size, natural selection sequence was proposed by Darwin and Wallace for organic evolution.
Overproduction: There is an overproduction of organisms due to high reproductive rate, even when the resources are limited. Even though the population increases enormously, the number of individuals in every generation remains constant.
Variation: means differences, like you have black and white peppered moths, red, green capsicum and hundreds of colours of butterflies. And they are all different because they are adapting themselves, to be better than each other.
Natural selection: It states that nature creates struggle and selects those animals which win in the competition. The organisms which have useful variations will win in the competition. Whereas the organisms which have no such useful variations will die.

Since, $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$is the image of the point $\left(1, - 2, 3\right)$ in the plane. So, we have,

$\dfrac{\alpha - 1}{2} = \dfrac{\beta + 2}{3} = \dfrac{\gamma - 3}{- 1} = \dfrac{- 2\left|2\left(1\right) + 3\left(- 2\right) - \left(3\right) - 7\right|}{\left({2}^{2} + {3}^{2} + {\left(- 1\right)}^{2}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha - 1}{2} = \dfrac{\beta + 2}{3} = \dfrac{\gamma - 3}{- 1} = \dfrac{- 2\left|2 - 6 - 3 - 7\right|}{4 + 9 + 1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha - 1}{2} = \dfrac{\beta + 2}{3} = \dfrac{\gamma - 3}{- 1} = - 2$

$∴ \dfrac{\alpha - 1}{2} = - 2 ⇒ \alpha = - 4 + 1 = - 3$

$\dfrac{\beta + 2}{3} = - 2 ⇒ \beta = - 6 - 2 = - 8$

and $\dfrac{\gamma - 3}{- 1} = - 2 ⇒ \gamma = 2 + 3 = 5$

So, $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = - 3 - 8 + 5 = - 6$

$r = 6Ω$

$∴ x = \dfrac{\left(2R + x\right) \times R}{\left(3R + x\right)}$
$⇒ x = \left(\sqrt{3} - 1\right) \times R$
$= \left(1.73 - 1\right) \times 100$
$= 73Ω$

92954.text: Two electrons in two hydrogen-like atoms $A$ and $B$ have their total energies ${E}_{A}$ and ${E}_{B}$ in the ratio ${E}_{A}: {E}_{B} = 1: 2$. Their potential energies ${U}_{A}$ and ${U}_{B}$ are in the ratio ${U}_{A}: {U}_{B} = 1: 2$. 92954.sol:
Given,

$\dfrac{{E}_{A}}{{E}_{B}} = \dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{{U}_{A}}{{U}_{B}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

So ${E}_{A} = x, {E}_{B} = 2x$

And ${U}_{A} = y, {U}_{B} = 2y$

$∵ {E}_{A} = {U}_{A} + {K}_{A}$

And ${E}_{B} = {U}_{B} + {K}_{B}$

here ${K}_{A}$ and ${K}_{B}$ are kinetic energy of particles $A$ and $B$

So ${K}_{A} = {E}_{A} - {U}_{A} = \left(x - y\right)$ .....(i)

${K}_{B} = {E}_{B} - {U}_{B} = 2 \left(x - y\right)$ ....(ii)

$∵$ de-Broglie wavelength,

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mk}}$

So ${\lambda}_{A} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m{K}_{A}}}, {\lambda}_{B} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m{K}_{B}}}$

$∴ \dfrac{{\lambda}_{A}}{{\lambda}_{B}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{K}_{B}}{{K}_{A}}} .....($ iii)

From Equation (i), (ii) and (iii),

$\dfrac{{\lambda}_{A}}{{\lambda}_{B}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\left(x - y\right)}{\left(x - y\right)}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{1}$

93112.text: The electric potential in a region is given as $V = – 4a{r}^{2} + 3b$, where $r$ is distance from the origin, $a$and $b$ are constants. If the volume charge density in the region is given by $ρ = na{ε}_{0}$, then what is the value of $n$?
93112.sol:
$V = - 4a{r}^{2} + 3b$

$E = \dfrac{- dV}{dr} = 8ar$

The small amount of flux $dϕ$ associated with the closed surface bounded by two spheres of radius $r$ and $r + dr$ is

$dϕ = \left(E + dE\right)\left(A + dA\right) - EA$

$dϕ = EdA + dEA$

$dE = 8adr$and $dA = 8\pirdr$

Using Gauss's law

$\dfrac{ρ \times 4\pi{r}^{2}dr}{{ε}_{0}} = 8adr \times 4\pi{r}^{2} + 8ar \times 8\pirdr$

⇒ $ρ = 24a{ε}_{0}$

$n = 24$

93835.text: Two trains $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ of length $\text{400 m}$ each are moving on two parallel tracks with a uniform speed of $72\dfrac{km}{h}$ in the same direction, with $\text{A}$ ahead of $\text{B}$. The driver of $\text{B}$ decides to overtake $\text{A}$ and accelerates by $1\dfrac{m}{s2}$. If after $\text{50 s}$, the guard of $\text{B}$ just brushes past the driver of $\text{A}$~and the original distance between them is $x$, then calculate value of $\dfrac{x}{10}$ ?
93835.sol:
Length of each train,

${l ⁡}_{A} = {l ⁡}_{B} = 4 0 0 \text{m}$

$u{⁡}_{A ⁡} = 72 \times \dfrac{5}{18}\text{m/s}$

$\text{= 20 m/s}$

Distance travelled by train $\text{A}$ in $\text{50 s}$

${s}_{A} = {u}_{A} \times \text{t}$

(As for unaccelerated motion, distance = Speed x Time)

${s}_{A} = 2 0 \times 5 0$

$\text{= 1000 m}$

Distance travelled by train $\text{B}$ in $\text{50 s}$,

${s}_{B} = {u}_{B} \text{t} + \dfrac{1}{2} {a}_{B} t^{2}$

(As motion of train B is an accelerated motion)

${s}_{B} = 2 0 \times 5 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times {\left(5 0\right)}^{2}$

$\text{= 1000 + 1250}$

$\text{= 2250 m}$

relative distance between the two trains ${\text{=S}}_{B} - {S}_{A}$

$\text{= 2250 - 1000}$

$\text{= 1250 m}$
we should subtract~$2l$ from it where $l$~is length of train so final answer will be 450 m

Alternate Method

Initially, both the trains are moving with same speed, the train $\text{B}$ first comes that of the train $\text{A}$ in $\text{50 s}$ with an acceleration of $\text{50 s}$.

$∴$ Original distance between the trains

= Distance covered by train $\text{B}$ with an acceleration a

$= \text{ut} + \dfrac{1}{2} {at}^{2}$

$= 0 \times 5 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times {\left(5 0\right)}^{2}$

(As both train starts with same velocity, so velocity, so velocity of train when it starts accelerating can be taken as zero).

$\text{= 1250 m}$ .

we should subtract $2l$ from it where $l$ is length of train so final answer will be $\text{450 m}$

95894.sol: The branch of science that deals with the naming and classification of living organisms on the basis of similarities and dissimilarities. is called taxonomy. 96825.text:
Read the following statements about a leaf. Which amongst them are correct?

I. The swollen leaf-base mainly seen in leguminous plants is called the pulvinus.
II. The axillary bud arises from the axil formed by the leaf.
III. The leaf lamina is generally flat but may vary in shape and size from plant to plant.
96825.sol: The leaf is the main photosynthetic organ of the plant. It majorly consists of the leaf base, petiole, and the leaf lamina. Sometimes the swollen leaf base, called pulvinus, is seen in leguminous plants. The leaf generally emerges from the node of the stem where it forms an axil through which an axillary bud emerges. This axillary bud further develops into a branch. The leaf lamina serves as the stage for harvesting light for photosynthesis. The shape of the leaf may vary from plant to plant

101386.subject: Physics
101386.text: A satellite orbits the Earth with a time period of $24\text{ h}$ at an orbital radius $R$. Another satellite orbits the Earth with a time period of $3\text{ h}$. The orbital radius of the second satellite is:
101386.sol:
According to Kepler's third law of planetary motion, the square of the time period of a satellite is directly proportional to the cube of its orbital radius.

$T^2 \propto R^3$

For the two satellites, we can write the ratio as:

$\left(\dfrac{R_2}{R_1}\right)^3 = \left(\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^2$

Given that $T_1 = 24\text{ h}$, $R_1 = R$, and $T_2 = 3\text{ h}$:

$\left(\dfrac{R_2}{R}\right)^3 = \left(\dfrac{3}{24}\right)^2$

$\left(\dfrac{R_2}{R}\right)^3 = \left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{64}$

Taking the cube root on both sides:

$\dfrac{R_2}{R} = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{1}{64}} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$R_2 = \dfrac{R}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{R}{4}$

105003.subject: Physics
105003.text: A heavy nucleus of mass number $64$ hypothetically breaks into $8$ identical lighter nuclei, each of mass number $8$. The ratio of the total surface area of all the $8$ lighter nuclei to the surface area of the original nucleus is:
105003.sol:
The radius of a nucleus is given by $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$.

The surface area of a nucleus is $S = 4\pi R^2$.

Substituting the expression for $R$, we get $S \propto A^{2/3}$.

For the original nucleus ($A = 64$), the surface area is:

$S_0 \propto (64)^{2/3} = 16$

For one lighter nucleus ($A' = 8$), the surface area is:

$S_1 \propto (8)^{2/3} = 4$

The total surface area of all $8$ lighter nuclei is:

$S_{\text{total}} = 8 \times S_1 \propto 8 \times 4 = 32$

The required ratio is:

$\dfrac{S_{\text{total}}}{S_0} = \dfrac{32}{16} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

Thus, the ratio is $2:1$.

Answer: $2:1$

106236.text:
Which of the following combination of statements is true regarding the interpretation of the atomic orbitals?
$( A )$ An electron in an orbital of high angular momentum stays away from the nucleus than an electron in the orbital of lower angular momentum.
$( B )$ For a given value of the principal quantum number, the size of the orbit is inversely proportional to the azimuthal quantum number.
$( C )$ According to wave mechanics, the ground state angular momentum is equal to $\dfrac{h}{2\pi}$ .
$( D )$ The plot of $ψ$ Vs $r$ for various azimuthal quantum numbers, shows peak shifting towards higher $r$ value.
106236.sol:
Statements (B) and (C) are incorrect.
For a given value of the principal quantum number, the size of the orbit is directly proportional to the azimuthal quantum number and not inversely proportional.
The formula for angular momentum is $\dfrac{h}{2\pi}\sqrt{l( l + 1 )}$  
If the electron is in ground state, n will be 1 and the only azimuthal quantum number value can be 0. If l = 0, angular quantum momentum will also be 0. The plot of $ψ$ Vs $r$ for various azimuthal quantum numbers, shows peak shifting towards higher $r$ value.

115428.text: The percentage of heat supplied to a diatomic ideal gas that is converted into work in an isobaric process is

For isobaric process, $\Delta \mathrm{p}=0\begin{aligned}
& \Delta \mathrm{W}=0 \\
& \Delta \mathrm{U}=\Delta \mathrm{Q}-\Delta \mathrm{W} \\
& =\Delta \mathrm{Q} \\
& \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}} \mathrm{dT}=\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{dT} \\
& \frac{\Delta \mathrm{U}}{\Delta \mathrm{Q}}=\frac{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}}}=\frac{\frac{5}{2} \mathrm{R}}{\frac{7}{2} \mathrm{R}}=\frac{5}{7}
\end{aligned}$
The percentage of heat supplied into work
$\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{5}{7} \times 100 \\
& =71.4 \%
\end{aligned}$

121718.subject: Botany
121718.text: What are members of Chlorophyceae commonly called?
121718.sol: The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus.<mark>The members of chlorophyceae are commonly called green algae</mark>. The plant body may be unicellular, colonial or filamentous. They are usually grass green due to the dominance of pigments chlorophyll a and b. The pigments are localized in definite chloroplasts. The chloroplasts may be discoid, plate-like, reticulate, cup-shaped, spiral or ribbon-shaped in different species. Most of the members have one or more storage bodies called pyrenoids located in the chloroplasts. Pyrenoids contain protein besides starch. Some algae may store food in the form of oil droplets. Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.

122205.subject: Botany
122205.text: What is the process called when cnidarians exist in both polyp and medusa forms?
122205.sol: Cnidarians exhibit tissue level of organization and are diploblastic. Cnidoblasts, also known as cnidocytes, contain stinging capsules or nematocysts and are used for anchorage, defense, and prey capture in cnidarians. Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa Cnidarians that exist in both polyp and medusa forms exhibit alternation of generation, where polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually. They have a central gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening, mouth on hypostome. Digestion is extracellular and intracellular. Some of the cnidarians, e.g., corals have a skeleton composed of calcium carbonate. Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa (Figure 4.6). The former is a sessile and cylindrical form like Hydra, Adamsia, etc. whereas, the latter is umbrella-shaped and free-swimming like Aurelia or jelly fish. Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (Metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually (e.g., Obelia).

122989.subject: Botany
122989.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the arrangement of ovules within the ovary in plants like sunflower and marigold?
options: The placenta is axial and ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary.
The placenta develops at the base of the ovary and a single ovule is attached to it.
The ovules are borne on the central axis and septa are absent.
The placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary and ovules are borne on this ridge.
122989.sol:
Sunflower and marigold exhibit basal placentation. In basal placentation, the placenta develops at the base of the ovary and a single ovule is attached to it.

The placenta being axial in a multilocular ovary describes axile placentation (e.g., tomato). Ovules borne on a central axis without septa describes free central placentation (e.g., Primrose). A placenta forming a ridge along the ventral suture describes marginal placentation (e.g., pea).

Answer: The placenta develops at the base of the ovary and a single ovule is attached to it.

123037.subject: Botany
123037.text:
Read the following statements carefully regarding the regions of the root:

Statement A: The region of meristematic activity is situated distal to the region of elongation.
Statement B: Cells of the elongation zone undergo rapid elongation and enlargement.
Statement C: Root hairs are multicellular epidermal structures arising from the maturation zone.
Statement D: The root cap is a thimble-like structure that protects the tender apex of the root.

How many of the above statements are correct?
123037.sol:
Statement A is correct: The region of elongation is proximal to the meristematic zone, which means the meristematic zone is distal (towards the tip) to the elongation zone.

Statement B is correct: The cells of the elongation zone undergo rapid elongation and enlargement, being responsible for the growth of the root in length.

Statement C is incorrect: Root hairs do arise from the maturation zone, but they are unicellular elongations of the epidermal cells, not multicellular. Multicellular epidermal hairs are typically trichomes found on the shoot system.

Statement D is correct: The root cap is a thimble-like structure covering the root apex to protect it as it penetrates the soil.

Therefore, exactly three statements (A, B, and D) are correct.

Answer: Only three

124278.subject: Botany
124278.text:
In a eukaryotic cell, Organelle 'X' is involved in the synthesis of proteins, which are then modified and packaged by Organelle 'Y'. Organelle 'Y' subsequently pinches off vesicles that mature into Organelle 'Z', which is rich in hydrolytic enzymes.

Which of the following statements correctly describes Organelle 'Z'?
options: It is a double membrane-bound structure containing its own circular DNA.
Its hydrolytic enzymes are optimally active at an alkaline pH.
It is excluded from the endomembrane system due to its independent functions.
It is a single membrane-bound vesicular structure whose enzymes are optimally active at an acidic pH.
124278.sol:
Based on the coordinated pathway described, Organelle 'X' is the Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER), which synthesizes proteins. These proteins are modified and packaged by Organelle 'Y', the Golgi apparatus. The Golgi apparatus pinches off vesicles that mature into Organelle 'Z', which are the lysosomes.

Lysosomes are single membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus. They are rich in hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases) that are optimally active at an acidic pH.

Option 1 is incorrect because lysosomes are single membrane-bound and lack DNA (unlike mitochondria and plastids).

Option 2 is incorrect because lysosomal enzymes require an acidic pH, not alkaline.

Option 3 is incorrect because lysosomes are a core component of the endomembrane system, as their functions are coordinated with the ER and Golgi complex.

Answer: It is a single membrane-bound vesicular structure whose enzymes are optimally active at an acidic pH.

Auxins are classified into natural and synthetic types. IAA (Indole-3-acetic acid) and IBA are natural auxins, whereas NAA and $2,4$-D are synthetic auxins.

Answer: X = $2,4$-D, Y = Dicotyledonous

125155.text: During a single turn of the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, there are exactly three points where $\text{NAD}^{+}$ is reduced to $\text{NADH} + \text{H}^{+}$. Which of the following represents the correct set of substrates that undergo oxidation at these three specific points?
options: Isocitrate, Succinic acid, and Malic acid
Citric acid, Succinic acid, and Fumaric acid
125155.sol:
In the TCA cycle, there are three specific steps where $\text{NAD}^{+}$ acts as an electron acceptor and is reduced to $\text{NADH} + \text{H}^{+}$. These steps involve the oxidation of the following substrates:
1. Isocitrate is oxidised to $\alpha$-ketoglutaric acid.
2. $\alpha$-ketoglutaric acid is oxidised to Succinyl-CoA.
3. Malic acid is oxidised to Oxaloacetic acid.

Succinic acid oxidation reduces $\text{FAD}$ to $\text{FADH}_{2}$, not $\text{NAD}^{+}$. The conversion of Succinyl-CoA to Succinic acid involves substrate-level phosphorylation, and Fumaric acid undergoes hydration to form Malic acid without oxidation.

Therefore, the correct set of substrates is Isocitrate, $\alpha$-ketoglutaric acid, and Malic acid.

Answer: Isocitrate, $\alpha$-ketoglutaric acid, and Malic acid

125419.subject: Botany
125419.text: How many carbon atoms does oxaloacetic acid (OAA) have?
125419.sol: Let us now ask ourselves a question that was asked by the scientists who were struggling to understand the ‘dark reaction’. How many carbon atoms would a molecule have which after accepting (fixing) CO2 , would have 3 carbons (of PGA)? The studies very unexpectedly showed that the acceptor molecule was a 5-carbon ketose sugar – ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP). Did any of you think of this possibility? Do not worry;Scientists also tried to know whether all plants have PGA as the first product of CO2 fixation, or whether any other product was formed in other plants. Experiments conducted over a wide range of plants led to the discovery of another group of plants, where the first stable product of CO2 fixation was again an organic acid, but one which had 4 carbon atoms in it. This acid was identified to be oxaloacetic acid or OAA.

125463.subject: Botany
125463.text: Why does photorespiration not occur in C4 plants?
options: They have a mechanism that increases the concentration of CO2 at the enzyme site
They only use O2 for respiration
125463.sol: In C4 plants photorespiration does not occur. This is because they have a mechanism that increases the concentration of CO2 at the enzyme site. This takes place when the C4 acid from the mesophyll is broken down in the bundle sheath cells to release CO2 – this results in increasing the intracellular concentration of CO2 . In turn, this ensures that the RuBisCO functions as a carboxylase minimising the oxygenase activity. Now that you know that the C4 plants lack photorespiration, you probably can understand why productivity and yields are better in these plants. In addition these plants show tolerance to higher temperatures.

125573.subject: Botany
125573.text:
ExperimentsFindings
A. Joseph Priestley's experiment with a candle and a mouse1) Air is restored by plants
B. Joseph Priestley's experiment with a mint plant2) Sunlight is necessary for releasing oxygen
C. Jan Ingenhousz's experiment with an aquatic plant in sunlight3) Candle extinguishes, mouse suffocates in closed jars
D. Jan Ingenhousz's experiment with aquatic plants in the dark4) Bubbles formed are oxygen
E. Plants in sunlight5) No bubbles formed, indicating lack of oxygen release
125573.sol:
A - 3: Joseph Priestley observed that in a closed bell jar, both the candle and mouse would suffocate or extinguish due to the depletion of oxygen, demonstrating that both combustion and respiration use up the air (oxygen).
B - 1: When Priestley placed a mint plant in the same bell jar, he found that the air was "restored," allowing the candle to burn again and the mouse to survive, showing that plants release a substance (oxygen) that restores the air.
C - 4: Ingenhousz's experiment with an aquatic plant showed that in bright sunlight, bubbles formed around the green parts of the plant. He identified these bubbles as oxygen, indicating that photosynthesis occurs in the presence of sunlight.
D - 5: In the absence of sunlight (dark conditions), Ingenhousz observed that no bubbles formed around the aquatic plant, indicating no oxygen release, and hence, no photosynthesis.
E - 2: Plants exposed to sunlight release oxygen, highlighting that sunlight is essential for the photosynthetic process that purifies the air.

125794.subject: Botany
125794.text: What is the function of the tapetum?
125794.sol: The bilobed nature of an anther is very distinct in the transverse section of the anther. The anther is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure consisting of four microsporangia located at the corners, two in each lobe. The microsporangia develop further and become pollen sacs. They extend longitudinally all through the length of an anther and are packed with pollen grains. Structure of microsporangium: In a transverse section, a typical microsporangium appears near circular in outline. It is generally surrounded by four wall layers the epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and the tapetum. The outer three wall layers perform the function of protection and help in dehiscence of anther to release the pollen. The innermost wall layer is the tapetum. It nourishes the developing pollen grains. Cells of the tapetum possess dense cytoplasm and generally have more than one nucleus. Can you think of how tapetal cells could become bi-nucleate?

126422.subject: Botany
126422.text: Based on cellular mechanisms there are two major types of regeneration found in the animals. Which one of the following is the correct example of the type mentioned?
options: Morphallaxis - Regeneration of two transversely cut equal pieces of a Hydra into two small Hydras
Epimorphosis - Replacement of old and dead erythrocytes by the new ones
Morphallaxis - Healing up of a wound in the skin
Epimorphosis - Regeneration of crushed and filtered out pieces of a Planaria into as many new Planarians
126422.sol:
Based on cellular mechanisms, regeneration can be divided into two broad categories : morphallaxis and epimorphosis.
Morphallaxis refers to the type of regeneration in which lost body parts are replaced by the remodelling of the remaining tissue. In this type of regeneration, little or no cellular proliferation takes place during the regeneration process. A classic example of an organism that regenerates using this mechanism is the Hydra. When a Hydra is cut into two pieces, two Hydra will be regenerated, both smaller than the parental Hydra. Once regeneration is completed, the two Hydra can continue to grow and reach the size of their original parent. In contrast to morphallaxis epimorphosis require active cellular proliferation prior to the replacement of the lost body part. For eg. Planarian, which are flatworms, regenerate using a mechanism in which pre-existing stem cells, known as neoblasts, begin to proliferate and migrate to the injured site in response to injury. These cells then form a mass of proliferating cells, known as regeneration blastema, that will later differentiate into the specialized cells that comprise the regenerated structure. Most tissue regeneration in mammals also belongs to the epimorphosis. For example, mammals can regenerate their muscle, bone epithelia of the skin and gut, blood, and some neurons by activating pre-existing stem cells or progenitor cells.
